rows: Weekly optimisation – week of Mon Nov 23 to Sun Nov 29

Set on Monday for the whole week; during the week only the tracking columns on the right change (one block per day: budget at end of day, spend, CPI or cost per purchase, and any change made that day). Objective: FVV / 3VV / 5VV / Install → lowest CPI; Purchase / RT → lowest cost per purchase. Baseline = Nov 16–22.

Roles – Keeper: best ad set of its group (lowest CPI / cost per purchase over 3 AND 7 days); receives budget from donors.  Donor: same group, worse – paused, budget moves to the keeper named in "Merge into".  Standalone: kept on its own – either the only ad set of its group, or same group but deliberately not merged (the Reference column says why).  Test: new ad / new bid / learning, judged on the check date.  Stop: paused, budget not moved.  Group = the show/creative the ad set actually spends on, not its name.

Lessons from the mergers so far

Worked when (a) the keeper was the more efficient ad set AND (b) the donor brought a genuinely new, strong creative into it – e.g. DelvsMum into Hisaab Barabar (T1019), Double Trouble into Baapu (T1019), HBBM_10min_Broad (F1014).

Failed when budget was added from donors that were worse than the keeper, or had zero purchases (most Oct 13 Purchase mergers). Moving a weak ad set's money into a keeper does not make that money efficient.
Jumps of 2.5x or more in one step mostly got worse, except where the keeper was clearly the best ad set.
Copied ads rarely get spend: Meta keeps budget on the keeper's existing winner, so "moving ads" only helps when the ad beats the keeper's current best ad.
Always pick the keeper by cost per result, not by size – on Oct 13 the best Purchase ad set (HBBM_2min_Interest, ₹170 per purchase) was paused as a donor.
